clue.text: Little fish flipping bit children

indicators.note: a bit is a binary digit, and flipping one turns a 1 into a 0, so a letter shaped like one becomes the letter shaped like nought

blocks.note: tiddlers are tiny fish, such as minnows caught by children

explanation.surface: Some small fish thrash about and nip a group of kids paddling.
explanation.walkthrough: TIDDLERS has an I, which looks like the digit 1; flip that bit to 0 and it reads as O, giving TODDLERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Toddlers are young kids just learning to walk, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Secret papers suppressed by hospital study

indicators.note: in a down entry, something suppressed by another is held underneath it, so it is written after

blocks.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
identity documents
a den is a private study or workroom

explanation.surface: Confidential documents are hushed up by a review into a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suppressed' sounds like a cover-up, which suits the surface, but in a down answer it simply says which piece sits lower.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hidden is kept out of sight, which is what a secret thing is; both adjectives describe concealment.

clue.text: Ill-informed rating managed to convey negative response

indicators.note: managed here means handled or worked over, so the letters before it are rearranged
to convey is to carry, so the reworked letters carry something inside them

blocks.note: taken as written
the word you answer with when refusing

explanation.surface: A poorly informed review score somehow managed to communicate a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant means lacking knowledge or awareness, the same sense as being poorly informed about something.

clue.text: Trained killer helping to make bureaucrat terrified

indicators.note: letters that help to make up a phrase are a part of it, so look inside the following words

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A trained assassin helps frighten an official out of his wits.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratter is a dog or cat kept and trained to catch and kill vermin, a killer by training.

clue.text: High toll can end in mourning

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a tin is a can of food
the closing letter of mourning

explanation.surface: A shrill death knell might complete a period of grieving.
explanation.definitionFit: A ting is a clear, high-pitched ringing sound, like a small bell being struck once.

clue.text: Fuel talk of avoiding loud row

indicators.note: a word avoiding something does without it, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: to gas is to chatter idly
taken as written
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a row of things is a line

explanation.surface: Chat about fuel that sidesteps a noisy argument.
explanation.walkthrough: F for loud is the musical marking forte; 'row' here is a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasoline is the American name for petrol, the liquid that powers car engines.

clue.text: Decoration America awarded to President finally includes servicemen

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the words that come before it
the selected letters include, or hold inside them, what follows

blocks.note: the final letter of each of the four words
RN, the Royal Navy, and its MEN

explanation.surface: A medal America conferred on the head of state goes at last to service personnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' reaches back over all four words America, awarded, to and President, not just the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: An adornment is an ornament or embellishment, something added for beauty, just as a decoration is.

clue.text: When one might eat lavishly, but only after fasting initially

indicators.note: but here means except, so the word survives only after something is removed
initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a feaster is someone eating lavishly
the opening letter of fasting

explanation.surface: A time for indulgent eating, permitted only once a fast is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the festival: it follows the Lenten fast and brings feasting. FEASTER loses its F.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is a date in the church calendar, a point in time answering the question of when something happens.

clue.text: A position where ball stops following attempt?

definitions.text: A position where ball stops following attempt?

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the pieces before it are placed later in the answer

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
taken as written
in golf, the lie is where the ball comes to rest

explanation.surface: A question about where a ball ends up after a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the keeper, whose position is where a ball on target is stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalie is a goalkeeper, the player stationed in the net to stop shots at goal.

clue.text: By playing three of diamonds one indicated support

indicators.note: playing cards are moved about and rearranged, so these letters are shuffled

blocks.note: D for diamonds, three times
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bridge player shows a partner support by leading a low diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds, so three of them are DDD rather than a card.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding the head is a gesture of agreement, so someone who nodded signalled their approval.

clue.text: Lack support to carry gun around

indicators.note: turned around, the word runs the other way
to carry something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to shore up is to prop or support
gat is old slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: Without backing, someone needs to carry a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is an insufficient amount of something, which is exactly what a lack of it means.

clue.text: Prisoner's means of communication curtailed by committee's conclusion

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the final letter goes
a conclusion is an end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the online network
the final letter of committee

explanation.surface: An inmate's lifeline to the outside is cut off by a committee's decision.
explanation.walkthrough: INTERNET loses its last letter, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is someone confined or detained, typically in wartime without trial, so a kind of captive.

clue.text: Distribute Remain flyers on a regular basis

indicators.note: to distribute is to spread out and scatter, so these letters are dispersed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Campaigners hand out pro-EU leaflets regularly, a picture of the Brexit referendum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyers' looks like leaflets in the surface, and 'on a regular basis' seems to describe the handing out, but both belong to the definition; Remain was the side wanting Britain to stay in the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen are members of an air force, people whose job is piloting or crewing aircraft routinely.

clue.text: Reputation turning into a tricky issue

indicators.note: turning round makes a word run backwards
tricky suggests something twisted or crafty, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: to make a name for oneself is to win a reputation
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A good reputation gets twisted into a problem matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that flows out from a source, which is one sense of an issue, as in an outflow.

clue.text: Standard space to print and write one's name

blocks.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
signing is writing your own name

explanation.surface: Instructions on a standard form: leave a gap for capitals, then sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag flown by a ship, and a standard is a flag or banner carried as an emblem.

clue.text: Person developing plot heartlessly rearranged broadcast

indicators.note: without its heart the word loses its central letters
broadcast seed is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A novelist working on a storyline has callously reshuffled a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten-letter word loses its middle two, RA, before being scrambled. 'Plot' suggests a story, but here it is a patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener cultivates a patch of land, so someone developing a plot of earth fits the description.

clue.text: Scheme to cut precious stone in multiple layers

indicators.note: cutting something out takes it away from the longer word

blocks.note: a stratagem is a cunning plan
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A jeweller's plan for cutting a gemstone into many layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers of rock or other material stacked one above another; the word is plural.

clue.text: Assuming success brought about out-and-out gains

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, like a ship changing tack, so the word reads backwards
a word that gains something takes it inside itself

blocks.note: arrant means utter, complete
to make a go of something is to make it a success

explanation.surface: Taking victory for granted, someone brings in outright profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assuming' is not the verb but the adjective meaning presumptuous; 'out-and-out' is a single synonym, not two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming can mean presumptuous or taking too much upon oneself, the same as being haughty and overconfident.

clue.text: Treating only one side of evidence is bad?

definitions.text: Treating only one side of evidence is bad?

indicators.note: treating something means processing it, so these letters are worked into another order
one side of a word is one of its edges, here the first letter

blocks.note: the leading letter of evidence
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether weighing only half the evidence is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes being partial; the wordplay uses its own words as raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Being biased means being prejudiced, considering only one point of view instead of weighing everything fairly.

clue.text: Old coin displayed by gallery in empty salver

indicators.note: something displayed by a frame is shown within it, so one piece goes inside the other
an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of salver
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: An ancient coin is exhibited in a museum on an empty serving tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A stater was a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece, so it is a historic piece of currency.

clue.text: Game in second half of June isn't shot

indicators.note: the second half of a word is its back half, so only those letters are kept
shot means ruined or wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: the back two of its four letters
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A sporting event late in June fails to get filmed, a nod to Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is played in late June, which is why the surface fits; 'shot' looks like a tennis stroke but scrambles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played over a net by two or four players, and so a kind of sport.

clue.text: Unable to pass time in debauched surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings enclose something, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: debauched means morally corrupt
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone serving a sentence in a squalid jail cannot get out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like getting through, but here means to pass away, to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone immortal lives forever and can never die, which is the euphemistic sense of pass.

clue.text: Nice lady cooked cakes in the morning

indicators.note: to cake something is to coat it thickly, so one piece is covered by the other

blocks.note: a meal you cooked is one you made
am, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A pleasant woman baked some pastries early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, so a Nice lady is a Frenchwoman; 'cakes' is a verb, not a bake.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French title for a married woman, the equivalent of a lady addressed in France.

clue.text: False reports of isolated people in the main wanting independence

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is missing from the longer word

blocks.note: the main is the sea, so these are people living cut off by it
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: Untrue stories about remote communities seeking self-rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanders are damaging untrue statements spoken about someone, so they are lying accounts.

clue.text: Characters imprisoned in dismal tower

indicators.note: only the letters locked inside the word survive, so its outer pair is dropped

blocks.note: dismal means dark and depressing

explanation.surface: Letters locked up in a grim tower, like a prisoner's carved initials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, to rise high above.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom is to rise up threateningly over something, just as a tall thing towers over its surroundings.

clue.text: Boy's best friend to stop working, packing nothing and going on vacation

indicators.note: packing means stuffing things inside, so the other pieces go within
a word on vacation has vacated its middle, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: a machine that dies stops working
zero
the first and last letters of going

explanation.surface: A lad's pet stops working, takes nothing and heads off on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Man's best friend is a dog, and the boy's version is the child's word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggie is the childish word for a dog, the animal proverbially called man's best friend.

clue.text: I regularly disobey guards close to second home

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
guards stand around what they protect, so the other pieces go inside
the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of disobey
the last letter of second
at home means in

explanation.surface: A rebellious lodger keeps flouting the rules near a second house.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the definition: I is the chemical symbol for this element.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the chemical symbol for iodine, a crossword-only sense letting a single letter stand for the element.

clue.text: Prevailing wisdom in anthropological circles

indicators.note: circles means surrounds, so the surrounding words hold the answer within them

blocks.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: The received wisdom among academics who study humanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevailing means most widespread or having the upper hand, as a dominant view or force does.
